body.x: ConTILab, led by CEO Park Chan-sik, participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas from January 9 to 12.

Established as an experimental company from the Construction Technology Innovation Lab at Chung-Ang University in 2022, ConTILab has been developing the industrial site safety accident prevention solution ‘iSafe’ platform to achieve ‘zero workplace accidents.’ The core of their technology is an artificial intelligence (AI) model that automatically identifies and assesses visible risk factors in industrial sites.

Their construction site risk detection solution, known as ‘iSafe-Guard,’ stands out with its specialized functionality in detecting potential risks that may occur during specific tasks, unlike conventional intelligent CCTV. Based on user requirements, the AI detector embedded in this solution can operate on various systems, such as cloud, server, edge, and mobile. It can also be linked to multiple video acquisition devices, including fixed and mobile CCTV, robots, and drones. Furthermore, beyond simple risk detection and notification methods, it offers information on safety levels for each task, showcasing excellent versatility as an industrial safety solution.

Additionally, iSafe-Meta creates a metaverse environment using 3D-Mesh generated from actual footage and images captured on-site. This provides a space for industry experts and workers to share insights.

User-generated content is rewarded with blockchain-based Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) to encourage the influx of many users. The solution also enables communication independent of nationality using ChatGPT and automatic translation features.

Through the iSafe solution, ConTILab successfully applied it to large-scale research projects of government agencies, seven construction projects, and two private construction projects last year, completing demonstrations in safety planning, education, and monitoring. Starting this year, ConTILab is in discussions with local departments to introduce iSafe to mandatory CCTV application sites in regional governments in South Korea, and they are planning to expand into overseas markets, starting with Southeast Asian countries such as Vietnam and Indonesia.

To become a global leader in the construction safety field and a ‘First Mover’ in safety management across all industries, ConTILab attended CES 2024. They conducted multiple meetings with domestic and international companies and institutions that showed significant interest in their solution for maintaining safety in various industrial sites.

ConTILab emphasized, “We were able to meet with domestic and international companies and institutions that showed great interest in our solution, which can maintain safety in various industrial sites,” and explained, “Our technology, utilizing over 120 self-developed AI algorithms to recognize objects and achieve automatic reading, seems to meet their needs.”

They added, “Investment institutions in the United States and Korea also visited ConTILab’s booth, expressing their intention to invest. As a result, we expect to accelerate the company’s growth even after the exhibition.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
